Adding a few technical clarifications so the token model is actionable:
- Batch sizing: our measured latency/throughput curve shows diminishing returns after batch size 8 for sequences ~400 tokens on our standard quantized runtime. For your median 420 tokens, sensible comparison rows: batch=1 (low latency), batch=4 (medium), batch=8 (high efficiency).
- Caching assumptions: prefix-KV is modeled as 20-30% token reuse for templated prompts (we'll run a quick prefix scan on your sample and refine). Session-level caching (for multi-turn flows) can push reuse to 45% in best case. Note: caching reduces tokens billed only when prefix+KV reuse avoids re-generation — there's also memory/latency tradeoff during spikes.
- Tokens per call: we'll model prompt+response tokens separately. You mentioned average response ~180 tokens; we'll use prompt=420 + response=180 = 600 total tokens per interaction baseline.

I'll produce the spreadsheet (nexavo_token_model.xlsx) with three scenarios, plus a one-page comparison chart and a short note about SLA fallback costs when we route to hosted variants under peak. Expect that in your inbox by EOD Thursday (Nov 27).

Jordan Blake
Product Strategy, Redwood Inference
